# Forsured

> Forsured is construction insurance compliance software. It checks every contractor certificate of insurance (COI) against a project's insurance requirements, flags coverage and endorsement gaps, brings the contractor's broker into the fix, and keeps checking for the life of the project. Built for general contractors, trade contractors and insurance brokers in the United States.

Key facts:
- Website: https://forsured.ai
- Contact: hello@forsured.ai
- Offer: a free COI risk check. Send one project's requirements and a contractor COI or two, and Forsured shows every gap it finds.
- Integrations: Procore (available for early access customers).

## Product

- [Forsured home](https://forsured.ai/): what Forsured does, how the review works, and who it's for (general contractors, brokers, trade contractors)
- [Free COI risk check](https://forsured.ai/#demo): send one project's requirements and a contractor COI

## Blog

- [A COI on file isn't proof of coverage](https://forsured.ai/blog/compliance-isnt-coverage/): A certificate of insurance shows what a contractor bought on one day. Here's what it can't tell you, and what to check against your project requirements instead.
- [3 takeaways from day 2 of IRMI's Construction Risk Conference](https://forsured.ai/blog/irmi-crc-2026-day-2-takeaways/): Additional insured endorsements, prequalification as a snapshot, and insurance data you can't search. What we were digging into on day 2 at IRMI CRC 2026.
- [IRMI is rewriting its design-build risk and insurance guide](https://forsured.ai/blog/irmi-design-build-guide-update/): IRMI picked American Global to rewrite its Design-Build Risk and Insurance guide. What the update covers, and what design-build means for contractor COI review.
- [How to check a contractor COI against your project requirements](https://forsured.ai/blog/how-to-check-a-contractor-coi/): A practical checklist for checking a contractor certificate of insurance against one project's requirements: coverages, limits, dates and endorsements.
- [3 takeaways from day 1 of IRMI's Construction Risk Conference](https://forsured.ai/blog/irmi-crc-2026-day-1-takeaways/): Crowded bids and thin margins, umbrella rates still rising, and contractor management turning into an underwriting factor. What stuck with us from day 1 at IRMI CRC 2026.
- [What the 2027 construction insurance outlook means for contractor COIs](https://forsured.ai/blog/construction-insurance-2027-renewal-outlook/): WTW forecasts construction umbrella and excess rates up 5% to 15% in 2027. Here's the full outlook by line, and why it raises the stakes on contractor COI review.
